what_was_said: Pledges and commitments across affected and high-risk countries total $498.8m

who: Africa CDC (Kaseya), via Reuters and Devex
what_was_said: Pledges 'almost halved' since Monday: from almost $500m to around $290m 'after some donors changed their minds' (Devex: $219m). Donors refused to let development funds be repurposed.

who: Africa CDC (Kaseya), via Health Policy Watch
what_was_said: 'Less than $2 million had reached affected countries despite pledges of around $498 million'
Groups working on the outbreak 'cannot tell where the money goes'; Kaseya did not know the size of the US contribution, what had been disbursed, or to whom

who: Africa CDC, after the AU High-Level Presidential Meeting
what_was_said: $910m in pledges mobilised; leaders called for the $518m plan to be funded within four weeks; Africa CDC to run a weekly commitment tracker of pledges and disbursements

who: Africa CDC (Kaseya), media briefing via Reuters
what_was_said: About $910m in funding pledges, 'but only 13% of that had been released'. Need revised to $1.4bn from $518m.

who: The Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response
what_was_said: 'As of June 22, the Africa CDC reports over $910 million in Ebola-specific pledges, yet under $90 million has been disbursed to countries and partners.' Warned of double counting between new and reprogrammed money and called for a published financing tracker.
Announced a $46m disbursement for the DRC Ebola response

who: Frontline responders, Ituri (Radio Okapi, Al Jazeera, AP)
what_was_said: Strikes at Rwampara treatment centre (Jul 13-14), Bunia General Hospital (Jul 15), street protest in Bunia (Jul 15-16), Elikya centre (Jul 25) over unpaid salaries and risk bonuses owed since May 15. Patients turned away; some died at home. Authorities said funding was not the cause and blamed administrative delays.
Continental plan 'still faces a funding gap of more than $400 million' of $518m
Government 'begins payment of bonuses' to health-zone and treatment-centre staff

Dozens protested at the governor's office over wages and bonuses unpaid since mid-May; several facilities abandoned. Minister said payments 'were being processed'. MSF said the protests concerned government compensation, not NGO pay. One worker reported $380 received against $510 promised.
Humanitarian health plan '62 percent funded'; OCHA 'had already received 35 million dollars from donors'; $80m 'used to kickstart the packages' and would run out within weeks
'More emergency funding has been disbursed' but 'it is not arriving quickly enough on the front lines'. No updated percentage.
Revised $2.13bn DRC humanitarian plan 48% funded; appeal for the remaining $1.1bn; resources 'will last weeks, not months'
More than $57m allocated through CERF for DRC and neighbouring countries

who: Responders in Damas health zone, Djugu, Ituri (Radio Okapi)
what_was_said: Response activities suspended; workers demand three months of risk bonuses and service payments plus regular PPE
$29.6m received of a $110m plan; 'less than a third'

Commitments reached about $2.9bn ($2.997bn), 'including around US$700 million announced in connection with the New York meeting'. Stressed this 'represents pledges, rather than money that has already been fully disbursed'. Africa CDC 'must trace every single dollar, from commitment to disbursement... to the services delivered'. Will enhance its Financial Tracking Mechanism.
DRC 'running short of health workers with Ebola out of control'; 'the health workers must be paid'

who: US State Department, G20 Chair's Statement
what_was_said: More than $470m in new commitments at the Sep 23 ministerial; total international pledges since May 'above $2 billion'. This tally is about $900m below Africa CDC's for the same event.

who: DRC Minister of Public Health Roger Kamba, press briefing
what_was_said: 'Only about 25% of the 97 partners present on the ground have justified the financial resources mobilised in favour of the DRC.' Announced mandatory declaration forms for all partners: 'no form, no accreditation; no accreditation, no access to the field'. On the first plan: about $227m mobilised, of which about $99m unused by partners; the state spent $50m of its own budget.

Called for 'rapid disbursement and full traceability' of the $2.9bn; 'every dollar must be traceable from the donor's commitment to the services delivered to communities'. Enhanced Financial Tracking Mechanism with the DRC government. No disbursed share given.
State Department 'has allocated $780 million... largely through NGOs' from funds already set aside by Congress; the $1.44bn supplemental is 'stuck in Congress'. No obligation or disbursement data.

who: A DRC responder on Democracy Now
what_was_said: Outstanding payments owed to colleagues for the first 45 days; WHO transport allowances covering 75 days still unsettled

US has 'announced' more than $887m; funds appear drawn from regular appropriations; Congress has not introduced legislation for the $1.44bn request; 'the full extent of WHO's outbreak funding is unclear'
